report_note: Height and weight alone should not support the same confidence as a full activity profile.

response.calorie_rationale: At 88 kg and lifting 5x/week, a modest calorie surplus is appropriate for muscle gain. Protein is set at about 1.7 g/kg, slightly above the 1.2–1.6 g/kg range cited for active lifters to support hypertrophy and recovery, while carbs are kept high to support training performance and glycogen needs.
response.meal_pattern: 3–5 meals per day with 25–40 g protein each, including a protein-forward meal or shake within a few hours after training. Spread carbs around workouts and keep meals consistent on training days.
foods_to_prioritize: Fruit and starchy carbs around workouts
foods_to_avoid: Protein foods with lots of added sugar
Ultra-processed add-on foods that crowd out nutrient-dense protein sources
response.sleep_note: Sleep matters for recovery and muscle gain; aim for consistent, sufficient sleep to support training adaptation and appetite regulation.
response.summary: This profile supports a lean bulk for an active 88 kg male lifting 5 times per week. Protein is prioritized to support muscle growth and recovery, with enough carbs to fuel training and replenish glycogen. Meals should be protein-centered and spread through the day, with carbs clustered around workouts. Emphasize minimally processed protein foods and watch key micronutrients that support performance and recovery.
